sec: PCR thresholds & 'also seen in' causes · p757

items.q: The bracket drawn after the 'Also seen in' causes carries which printed advice?
opts: Rx: Loop diuretics and salt restriction
items.exp: Nephrotic-range proteinuria is also seen in diabetes (m/c), secondary FSGS and amyloidosis, and the bracket beside that group reads 'Rx: ACE inhibitors, ARB'. (Book p757)

items.q: A raised urine protein–creatinine ratio is explicitly described on this page as not diagnostic of nephrotic syndrome.
opts: True — 'Not diagnostic of nephrotic syndrome' is printed under the PCR values
False — PCR alone defines nephrotic syndrome in children
False — the page says PCR replaces the 24-hour collection
items.exp: The PCR block gives adult ≥3000 mg/g and children ≥2000 mg/g, then the line 'Not diagnostic of nephrotic syndrome'. (Book p757)

items.q: A diabetic with a urine PCR of 4200 mg/g has serum albumin 3.8 g/dL and no edema. Per this page, the correct reading is:
opts: Nephrotic-range proteinuria that is not nephrotic syndrome, and the listed Rx is ACE inhibitors or ARBs
Nephrotic syndrome, since the PCR crosses 3000 mg/g
Nephrotic syndrome, because diabetes is the m/c associated cause
Neither — the PCR cannot be interpreted in diabetes
items.exp: The criteria demand nephrotic-range proteinuria with hypoalbuminemia and/or edema; the 'Also seen in' block names diabetes (m/c) with the bracketed advice 'Rx: ACE inhibitors, ARB'. (Book p757)
